conflicts.fact: Name of the girl in the anchoring phenomenon
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 2 and 5 call her Amara/Amina; Lessons 3, 4 and 7 call her Aisha. The phenomenon does not name her. Lesson 1 even uses both Amara and Amina.

conflicts.fact: Lesson in which the road-safety junction-mirror inset was added to the model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the inset was added in Lesson 3, but Lesson 3 does not mention any junction-mirror sketch. Lesson 6 introduces the junction-mirror context for the first time.

conflicts.fact: When the cumulative model was started
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1 and 2 say the model was started in Lesson 1. Lesson 7 says learners have been building it since Lesson 2.

Lesson 4 models the driver's side mirror as the y-axis and the rear-view mirror as the x-axis. Lesson 5 calls the matatu mirror a side mirror. Lesson 7 says the matatu rear-view mirror and describes a convex junction mirror with the same plane-mirror properties.

conflicts.fact: Aisha's total distance from her image and her position in the mirror
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says Otieno's total distance from his image is 2.4 m, with no mention of 6 m. Lesson 4 refers to a Lesson 2 calculation of '2 × 3 = 6 m total distance' for Aisha.

conflicts.fact: Position of the mirror in Lesson 4's Aisha model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 places Aisha at x=3 with the mirror at x=0, so her image is at x=−3 and the total distance is 6 units. Lesson 2 gave measured distances in cm (20–80 cm) and used Otieno with 2.4 m.
